subject: Creativity
title: Six Thinking Hats: Structured Perspective-Switching
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Six Thinking Hats: Structured Perspective-Switching.

hook.text: De Bono assigned thinking styles to colored hats: White=facts, Red=emotions, Black=caution, Yellow=optimism.

buildup.text: In meetings, people argue because they think from different perspectives simultaneously. Hats separate perspectives.

discovery.text: Everyone wears the same hat at the same time. This eliminates ego battles — you're playing a role, not defending a position.

twist.text: The Black Hat (criticism) is the most overused in business. Teams spend 90% of time criticizing, 10% creating.

climax.text: When teams use all six hats equally, meeting time drops by 75% and decision quality rises — proven in corporate studies.

punchline.text: Wear a different hat. Get a different idea.

quiz.question: What does the Green Hat represent in de Bono's Six Thinking Hats?

details.summary: De Bono's Six Thinking Hats assigns different colored hats to different thinking modes: facts, emotions, caution, benefits, creativity, and process. By wearing one hat at a time, groups avoid arguments and explore issues from all angles systematically.
details.whyItMatters: Six Thinking Hats prevents meetings from becoming unproductive debates. It ensures every perspective gets airtime and separates ego from ideas, making group thinking dramatically more effective.
takeaways: Each hat represents a distinct thinking mode or perspective
The method prevents individuals from defending fixed positions
Switching hats together ensures parallel rather than adversarial thinking

faq.question: What do the six hat colors represent?
faq.answer: White is facts and data, red is emotions and intuition, black is caution and risks, yellow is benefits and optimism, green is creativity and new ideas, and blue is process management and organization.

faq.question: Do you need to use all six hats every time?
faq.answer: No. You can select the hats most relevant to the situation. Some problems need more green hat creativity while others need more black hat risk assessment. The blue hat decides which sequence to use.
